Here's an issue I just ran into that people might find amusing:

import Mathlib

namespace Asymptotics

open Filter

/-- error: Unknown identifier `principal` -/
#guard_msgs in
#check principal
/-- info: Filter.principal.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s : Set α) : Filter α -/
#guard_msgs in
#check Filter.principal

But if we swap the namespace and the open, it works fine:

import Mathlib

open Filter

namespace Asymptotics

/-- info: Filter.principal.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s : Set α) : Filter α -/
#guard_msgs in
#check principal
/-- info: Filter.principal.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s : Set α) : Filter α -/
#guard_msgs in
#check Filter.principal
This happens because docs#Asymptotics.Filter.Tendsto.isBigOTVS_one exists. This is a feature of dot notation.

Just asking because Im pretty new and want to make sure I am doing it correctly:

All my namespaces are using dot notation (when applicable), and all of my open statements precede the namespace. This is correct Mathlib standards, yes?

oh its a funny issue with the namespace messing with the open statement into Mathlib? Ok.

Can/should we check for such naming collisions, e.g. Foo.Bar also existing in some other namespace Baz.Foo.Bar? (I'm not suggesting to ban these, but it might be useful to consciously look at existing collisions.)

Previous discussion (included code to find examples): #mathlib4 > TopLevelA.TopLevelB
Also #new members > generalized field notation vs namespaces is a user requesting such a feature.
